summary.text: Greg Steube is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for the 17th District, in office since January 2019. An attorney and Army veteran, he served in the Florida House and Senate before his election to Congress and sits on the Ways and Means and Intelligence committees. His official biography highlights his military service, work for seniors and agriculture, and conservative immigration positions.

paragraphs.text: Born in Manatee County, Florida, in 1978 (Wikipedia gives a birth date of May 19, 1978).
Earned his bachelor's degree (2000) and law degree (2003) from the University of Florida.
Enlisted in the U.S. Army while in law school, according to his official biography, and served as an airborne infantry officer and judge advocate general in the Army, 2004–2008.

According to his official biography, after an injury in Ranger school he transferred to the Army JAG Corps and served as Chief of Detainee Operations for Multinational Division North in Iraq with the 25th Infantry Division from 2006 to 2007, then as a JAG prosecuting courts-martial.
Served in the Florida House of Representatives from 2010 to 2016 and in the Florida State Senate from 2016 to 2018.
Won election to the U.S. House in 2018 and took office in January 2019, succeeding Rep. Thomas Rooney; he is seeking re-election in 2026 after an uncontested Republican primary.

Serves on the House Committee on Ways and Means (Health and Trade subcommittees) and the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence in 2025–2026; earlier served on Veterans' Affairs, Oversight, Judiciary and Foreign Affairs.
His official biography says he lives in Sarasota with his wife, Jennifer, and their son.
